title: OFR reports AI-enabled efficiency alongside lower staffing and changing public financial-data infrastructure
source_unit: Office of Financial Research FY2025 institutional annual-report self-report

denominator.unit: OFR employees at FY2024 starting point

observations.method: OFR annual-report self-report of workforce, budget, deferred-resignation participation, and organizational changes.
observations.uncertainty: The report does not attribute the workforce change to AI alone; it describes administrative priorities, rebalancing, limited travel/contractors/training/data procurement, and AI-enabled efficiency together. It does not measure service quality or workload per employee.
observations.subgroup: OFR workforce and organizational functions; no public subgroup outcome is reported.
observations.counterinterpretation: Lower staffing can reflect mission reprioritization or administrative policy rather than automation productivity; a smaller workforce may preserve or reduce analytical capacity depending on workload and tools.

observations.period: FY2025; OFR AI and analytics infrastructure inventory

denominator.unit: OFR institutional infrastructure and use-case inventory

ai_use_cases.value: data processing, security monitoring, support tasks, procurement comparison, and ChatOFR

analytics_platform_change.value: JADE decommissioned; OFRAE retained as core analytics environment

infrastructure.value: updated cloud-based service offerings and specialized operating system for analytics workflows

observations.method: OFR annual-report narrative on Artificial Intelligence and Automation and Technology and Core Analytics Infrastructure.
observations.uncertainty: Self-reported use cases and platform changes do not establish efficiency magnitude, model accuracy, staff workload, public benefit, data portability, or vendor dependence.
observations.subgroup: OFR analytical, security, support, procurement, and data-infrastructure functions.
observations.counterinterpretation: AI and cloud tools may augment staff while increasing review, security, or data-governance obligations; decommissioning one platform may simplify or reduce interagency collaboration.

observations.period: FY2025; new OFR non-centrally cleared bilateral repo data collection

denominator.unit: approximate dollars in daily outstanding commitments across the reported NCCBR market segment

nccbr_market_scale.unit: approximate U.S. dollars daily outstanding commitments

data_gap_status.value: new data made available to regulators for the first time

observations.method: OFR annual-report description of new non-centrally cleared bilateral repurchase-agreement data collection and its use during market volatility analysis.
observations.uncertainty: The approximate market amount is not a household exposure, firm market-power estimate, or realized stability improvement. Data availability does not establish that regulators prevented a disruption.
observations.subgroup: US financial institutions, market participants, regulators, and collateral types in the NCCBR segment.
observations.counterinterpretation: More data can improve monitoring while also increasing operational, privacy, and interpretation burdens; a large market segment is not necessarily unstable.

related_sources.claim: OFR publishes the FY2025 annual-report landing page and report context.
OFR provides public financial-data and monitoring context for its data-capacity mission.
Registered OFR institutional landing page for the source family and mission context.

boundary: This record captures OFR's FY2025 self-reported workforce, budget, AI use, analytics-platform, and financial-data-capacity changes. It does not establish that AI caused the staffing change, increased productivity by a measured amount, improved public service, reduced financial risk, or changed household or market outcomes. It is an institutional capacity and governance record.
